newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary 97 draft budget sees HUF361.7 bln deficit.
newsitem.headline: Hungary 97 draft budget sees HUF361.7 bln deficit.

text.p: Hungary's draft 1997 central state budget, not including one-off revenues such as proceeds from privatisation, targets a deficit of 361.7 billion forints, compared with the 1996 target of 232.9 billion forints, the Finance Ministry said on Monday.
The budget revenue target for 1997, not including one-off revenues, is 2,195.8 billion forints, expenditures are targeted at 2,557.5 billion forints.
Hungary plans to generate privatisation revenues of 60 billion forints next year.

The privatisation revenue target for 1996 was 100 billion forints, but by the end of August Hungary had already generated 192 billion forints from privatisations and expected a further 60 to 100 billion forints by the end of the year.
The central state budget does not include state funds and local municipalities.
Hungary earlier said that the deficit of its wider state budget is likely to amount to some 390 billion forints next year, or 4.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).

This is up from this year's four percent target because of a technical change in the accounting of foreign debt, but using the same method of calculation, the general government deficit will drop to three percent of GDP next year, Hungary said.
The central state budget will take over part of the foreign debt from the central bank from 1997.
The Finance Ministry said the central state budget will pay 834.6 billion forints in interest on the state debt in 1997, up from the 546.6 billion forecast for this year.
